newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Ousted Indonesian MP said detained for subversion.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Indonesian MP said detained for subversion.

text.p: Sacked Indonesian legislator Sri Bintang Pamungkas, ousted from parliament and convicted of defaming President Suharto, has been detained on subversion charges, his wife said on Thursday.

An intelligence official in the attorney-general's department, who refused to be named, confirmed Bintang and two other leaders of his fledgling United Democratic Party of Indonesia (PUDI) were in the department's detention.
However, he declined to give any further details. A departmental spokesman was not immediately available.

Bintang's wife Erna told Reuters her husband was officially detained late on Wednesday along with lawyer Julius Usman, secretary-general of the unrecognised PUDI, and leading member Saleh Abdullah, on subversion charges.
Subversion carries the death penalty in Indonesia.
"He was telephoned at 8 a.m. (on Wednesday) by officials from the attorney-general's office and told they wanted to discuss PUDI and his agenda on his Eid al-Fitr card," Erna said.
Bintang wrote PUDI's three-point agenda on cards sent last month to mark the Moslem festival of Eid al-Fitr.
The agenda calls for a boycott of the 1997 election, rejection of Suharto's re-election and the preparation for a new post-Suharto order after the 1998 presidential election.
Bintang sent the cards to numerous people, including vice-president Try Sutrisno, armed forces headquarters, the attorney-general and all cabinet ministers.
Erna said the three men went voluntarily to the attorney-general's office and Bintang telephoned in the evening to confirm he had been detained.
"The letter of detention had not yet been completed but there was already an order that he be detained by the President because he rejected the general election," she said.
The Kompas daily said another two PUDI members, its advisory board head Butje Rumaneri and Jus Soemadipraja, were also questioned on Wednesday, but their whereabouts were unknown.
A diplomat following Bintang's case said the order for the detention of Bintang and his colleagues may have come from Suharto.

The High Court last month upheld a lower court decision to sentence Bintang last May to 34 months in jail for defaming Suharto in a speech to Indonesian students in April 1995. He had remained out of jail pending a further appeal.

Bintang and Usman last October made a self-declared bid for the presidency and vice-presidency even though the constitution does not recognise such outside challenges for the post, which is decided every five years by an electoral college of parliament.
Suharto has been re-elected unchallenged for six consecutive terms since 1968 and is thought likely to run for another term next year.
"Bintang recognises what he is doing is getting in deeper and deeper. He's crossed the line, knows it and therefore is prepared to do things other people would tremble at," the diplomat said.
Bintang was sacked by the Moslem-orientated United Development Party (PPP) in 1995 for being too outspoken. The decision was subsequently approved by Suharto.

He founded his new party days after his conviction last year in defiance of government claims that Indonesia only has three recognised political parties, the ruling Golkar, the PPP and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
